title: Session
description: REVIEW REQUIRED — encodes the research decision of what describes a session. A normalized, content-free record of one agent session. Validated structurally against real Claude Code JSONL logs (~/.claude/projects/, format version 2.x, 20 sessions) and Cursor's ai-code-tracking.db on 2026-08-07; Codex rollout JSONL structurally validated 2026-08-09 (ADR-0004), so x-provenance claims now cover all three first-class sources. 0.3.0 (ADR-0004): provenance gains required content_hash + source_artifacts (extractor traceability); models[].assistant_messages no longer required (Cursor attributes lines, not messages); tokens gains reasoning_output (observed in Codex token_count); new nullable fork_of (fork/resume dedup, ADR-0002 finding 4); provenance.log_format gains cursor_state_db usage for composer-derived records. No content-level fields: no prompts, no code, no file contents, no stdout.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was written against. v0.x until post-interview revision.

session_id.description: Stable session identifier. Claude Code: the sessionId UUID (also the log filename). Cursor: conversationId from ai-code-tracking.db.

source_tool.description: Which agent harness produced the session. New harnesses enter as 'other' (with source_tool_other set) and are promoted to first-class enum values once a connector exists and their log format has been structurally validated in an ADR — see ADR-0003.

source_tool_other.description: Raw harness name when source_tool='other' (null otherwise), so 'other' traffic stays disaggregatable per harness instead of pooling into one bucket.

provenance.description: How this record was extracted — kept so any number is traceable to a log format, source artifact, and connector version.

log_format.description: 'codex_jsonl' is the rollout-*.jsonl format under ~/.codex/sessions/, structurally validated in ADR-0004. 'other' covers not-yet-promoted harnesses; source_format_version identifies the actual format.

source_format_version.description: The producing tool's own version (Claude Code logs carry `version` on every record; Codex session_meta carries cli_version). Real logs show fields appearing/disappearing across CLI versions — e.g. promptSource is present in 2026-08 sessions, null in 2026-07 sessions — so this field is load-bearing for parsing.

content_hash.description: sha256 (hex, 'sha256:' prefix) over the exact source content this record was derived from: the log file bytes for JSONL sources, a canonical serialization of the contributing rows for DB sources. The extractor's idempotency/dedupe key: an unchanged hash means the record is not rewritten.

source_artifacts.description: Every source file read to produce this record. Paths are local to the machine of extraction; extracted artifacts stay out of version control (data/README.md).

path.description: Path of the original artifact (for DB sources: the live DB path; extraction reads a snapshot copy).

sha256.description: sha256 of the artifact as read (for DB sources: of the snapshot copy).

rows.description: For DB sources: number of rows contributing to this record.

fork_of.description: session_id of an earlier-started session sharing this session's first user-prompt record UUID — a fork/resume artifact (ADR-0002 finding 4: identical records appear in multiple session files). Consumers must not double-count activity across a fork family. Null when no fork detected; absence of the signal is null, never a guess.

project_ref.description: Opaque project identifier (salted hash of cwd / repo root). Raw paths never leave the connector. Claude Code: derived from `cwd`.

git_branch.description: Branch at session time (`gitBranch` on every conversational record). Null when not in a repo.

started_at.description: Timestamp of the first stamped record.

ended_at.description: Timestamp of the last stamped record. IMPORTANT: real logs have NO end-of-session marker; a session file is appended to across resumes. Observed sessions span up to 5 days of wall clock. This is 'last activity seen', not 'session ended'.

end_observed.description: Always false for Claude Code logs (no end marker exists). Kept explicit so downstream duration math cannot silently treat ended_at as authoritative.

wall_clock_ms.description: ended_at - started_at. Misleading on its own (includes idle days); reported only alongside active_duration_ms.

active_duration_ms.description: Sum of system/turn_duration records (`durationMs`), which real logs emit per turn. The honest work-time signal. Null if the producing CLI version emitted no turn_duration records.

interrupted_tool_calls.description: Count of toolUseResult.interrupted == true — user cancelled mid-run. A human-friction signal.

tool_call_pattern.description: Per-tool call counts from tool_use blocks. MCP tools keep their mcp__<server>__ prefix so server-level bucketing is possible without content.

models.description: Every model that served part of the session (real sessions mix models: primary + fallback + '<synthetic>' bookkeeping records, which connectors must filter or label).

assistant_messages.description: Distinct assistant messages served by this model. ABSENT/null for sources that attribute work to a model without message granularity (Cursor's tracking DB attributes lines) — relaxed from required in 0.3.0, ADR-0004.

effort.description: Reasoning effort setting (`effort` field, e.g. 'high'). Present only in newer log versions — null means unrecorded, not 'default'.

tokens.description: Summed from per-message `usage`. Cache fields are first-class because real traffic is dominated by cache reads — cost models that ignore them are wrong.

input.description: Non-cached input tokens. Claude logs report this bucket directly (input_tokens excludes cache); Codex input_tokens INCLUDES cached_input_tokens, so the connector stores input_tokens - cached_input_tokens here to keep buckets non-overlapping across sources (ADR-0004).

reasoning_output.description: Reasoning tokens, observed in Codex token_count events (reasoning_output_tokens). A SUBSET of output, not an additional bucket — do not add it to output. Absent where the source does not report it (Claude Code, Cursor). Added 0.3.0, ADR-0004.

cost_usd.description: NOT in any real log. Computable only as tokens x an external price sheet, so it carries its pricing source or stays null.

diff_stats.description: Aggregated from structuredPatch hunks on Edit/Write tool results (verified present in real logs). Null when the session produced no edits.

user_modified_edits.description: Count of edits where the log's userModified flag is true — the human touched the AI's edit. Direct human-in-the-loop evidence; feeds attribution.

languages.description: File extensions touched, mapped to languages. Extension-based only — never inferred from content.

subagents.description: Real logs nest subagent transcripts under <session-id>/subagents/. Parent-session stats EXCLUDE subagent activity; each subagent may be its own session record with parent_session_id set.

parent_session_id.description: Set when this record describes a subagent transcript.

prompt_source_counts.description: Counts of user messages by origin (`promptSource`: typed / etc.; origin.kind: human / automated). Only in newer log versions — null means the producing version didn't record it. Distinguishes human-driven from scheduled/autonomous sessions.

segments.description: Contiguous runs of user-prompt turns, split by OBSERVABLE boundaries only — turn gaps, git branch changes, jumps to a disjoint file set, interruptions. No semantic/content inference in v0. Boundary rules are versioned as segmenter_version and documented in docs/conventions.md; segments from different segmenter versions are not comparable. Null only when segmentation has not been run. The classification UNIT (prompt vs segment vs session) is an open research question — see task_class.schema.

turn_range.description: Inclusive, over user-prompt turn indices as defined in conventions.md.

opened_by.description: The observable boundary that opened this segment. When several rules fire on the same turn, precedence is turn_gap > branch_change > file_set_jump > interrupt (conventions.md).

team_ref.description: Opaque team identifier. Not in any local log; comes from enterprise org mapping. Required for team-level reporting; null in synthetic and pre-deployment data is expected. Never resolves to an individual.

patches_accepted.description: Accept/reject counts as a first-class field exist in NEITHER real source (Cursor tracks source-of-lines, not accept events; Claude Code has userModified/interrupted as weaker proxies). Null until a telemetry export provides it.
